races.title: State Senate, District 46
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Warren Daniel
cands.bio: Republican state senator for North Carolina's District 46, serving since 2011. West Point graduate (1991) and Army field artillery officer for six years. UNC law graduate (2000), practicing attorney at the family law firm in Morganton. Has chaired Senate Judiciary and Appropriations committees.

endorsements.text: His campaign site says he is endorsed by NC Right to Life. This is his own claim, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birth city. We found no record of his positions on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, or limits on foreign or investor land buying. We found no specific bills or actions on any of those topics, or on school choice or teacher pay, policing or pensions, or H-1B visas. The Second Amendment, abortion and immigration items come only from his own campaign site and are not backed by official records. His campaign site did not say whether he supports school vouchers or charters.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site says he is a North Carolina native raised in Burke County, and he returned to Morganton to practice law in 2000.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2011 (about 15 years), including Senate Appropriations and Finance committee service. Practicing attorney since 2000 and small business owner at the Daniel Law Firm. Former U.S. Army field artillery officer (1991-1997).
qual.why: Long prior legislative service and a law career fit the work of writing law and the state budget. Committee chair posts were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Long prior legislative service and a law career fit the work of writing law and the state budget. Committee chair posts were not counted toward the score.

pro-life.evidence: Says human life deserves protection from conception to natural death, opposes taxpayer-funded abortion, and says he supported the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Act.

second-amendment.evidence: Says he holds an 'A' rating from the NRA, has fought to protect Second Amendment rights, and worked to pass a Castle Doctrine law.

workers-first.evidence: Says he will fight to overturn laws that weakened illegal-immigration enforcement, opposes government benefits and in-state community college tuition for illegal aliens, and wants local law enforcement to have the tools it needs.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

roots.summary: His campaign site says he is a North Carolina native raised in Burke County, and he returned to Morganton to practice law in 2000.

cands.name: Kyle Whisnant
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 46 in 2026. He advanced without a primary and lost the general election to incumbent Republican Warren Daniel. The sources available give no information on his career or any offices held.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from four Sway voting groups: Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress (Vote for Peace), Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy, Waves of Democracy, and Western NC Be Votin'.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, when he moved to North Carolina, or his occupation and work history. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. We found no campaign platform statements, interviews or questionnaires, so we could not document his stated positions on data centers, development, taxes, guns, abortion, immigration, schools or policing. We also found no record of official actions or news coverage about him, and nothing on controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No occupation, work history or prior office could be found in the available source.
qual.why: The background could not be established, so no score is given.
